proposed_genuine_additions.proposed_question: The Marquise attacks at the Keep with two warriors. The defender plays an unfoiled matching ambush, removing both attacking warriors. The Marquise can pay Field Hospitals. Are the warriors returned before or after the check that ends battle for having no attackers, and does battle continue if Hospitals is paid?
proposed_genuine_additions.expected_answer: The Marquise may immediately spend a matching card to return those warriors to the Keep clearing. This happens before the ambush checks whether attacking warriors or pawns remain. With the warriors returned, that early-ending condition is not met and battle continues. Without paying, if no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends after the ambush.
proposed_genuine_additions.material_new_branch: Priority of Hospitals return versus post-ambush no-attacker check changes whether battle reaches the roll; this is not an alternate casualty count.
proposed_genuine_additions.why_not_already_requested: Q03 asks the ordinary ambush early-ending rule; Q08 asks how Hospitals works without asking this subsequent battle-state check. Q22 forbids ordinary interrupts and Q69 assigns ordering among effects; neither identifies this mandatory immediate removal-trigger resolution before a separate no-attacker test. None of their fixed keys gives the distinguishing continuation result.

existing_target_key_findings.frozen_expected_answer: Placement and pawn-only movement do not trigger warrior-entry Outrage. Moving allied warriors there does trigger it.
existing_target_key_findings.issue: Blanket allied-warrior-entry trigger contradicts official FAQ when the forced Allied warriors belong to Woodland Alliance. It also omits attribution to the faction forced to move.
existing_target_key_findings.proposed_corrected_answer: Placement does not trigger warrior-entry Outrage. Vagabond pawn-only movement does not trigger it. When the Vagabond forces Allied warriors to accompany its pawn, resolve their move as if that Allied faction chose it. Forced Allied Alliance warriors entering sympathy do not trigger Outrage, because the Alliance is moving its own warriors. Forced warriors of another Allied faction entering sympathy do trigger Outrage for that faction: it gives one matching hand card, treating a bird as matching if required; if it has none, it shows its hand and the Alliance draws a supporter. The no-base five-supporter cap and overflow rule still apply. Vagabond removing sympathy still triggers Outrage independently of pawn movement.
existing_target_key_findings.explicit_vs_derived: No Outrage for forced Alliance warriors is explicit FAQ. The other-faction payer is application of 1.5.5 exactly-as-if-that-player-chose with 8.2.6 another-player-moves/they-must-pay; it is not a separately quoted FAQ sentence.

existing_target_key_findings.issue: Q20 requests coalition eligibility and partner selection, but fixed key does not exclude an already-activated dominance player from coalition selection. Official FAQ explicitly excludes them because they have no score marker on track.
existing_target_key_findings.proposed_key_addendum: A player who has already activated dominance cannot be chosen as coalition partner, because their score marker is not on the track. An existing coalition partner may later activate dominance under normal conditions; if they win that way the coalition victory linkage still applies.
